hints.title: Superimposed Node Fusion Obstacle
hints.text: When two trees overlap at corresponding positions, their values sum together. What should happen when one tree has a node at a position where the other tree has a null child?

hints.title: Disjoint Subtree Conservation Invariant
hints.text: If one node is null, the merged result at that position is simply the other non-null node. If both exist, sum their values and recurse on both pairs of children.

hints.title: Simultaneous Merge Traversal Procedure
hints.text: If root1 is null, return root2. If root2 is null, return root1. Create a new node with val = root1.val + root2.val (or reuse root1). Recursively merge left children into node.left and right children into node.right. Return the merged root.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Traversing overlapping nodes once with call stack bounded by the smaller tree height.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Creating full copies of non-overlapping subtrees instead of reusing references adds redundant time and memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Returning the other node immediately when one of the trees is null.
